firstMessage:
Login now throws `LockedError` on the fifth failed attempt, the one that sets the lock. Earlier failures still throw `BadCredentialsError`. The full suite passes (36/36), including the updated lockout test.

The change is in `src/accounts.ts`, where the lock is set. I also updated `src/accounts.test.ts` so the lockout test expects `BadCredentialsError` for the first four failures and `LockedError` for the fifth. Nothing is committed.

One trade-off to decide on: this makes the lock visible to anyone, including someone guessing passwords. An unregistered email never gets `LockedError`, so five wrong guesses now show whether an email has an account. Before, that took a correct password. If you want to avoid that, the lock message could be the same for every email, or you could return `LockedError` only after a correct password. Say if you want either.
finalMessage:
I read "yes, go ahead" as accepting the change with the trade-off as it stands, so I haven't added a mitigation. The change is done and the suite passes (36/36). It is uncommitted in the working tree.

The diff is in `src/accounts.ts`, which now throws `LockedError` on the fifth failed login, and `src/accounts.test.ts`, which expects `BadCredentialsError` for the first four failures and `LockedError` for the fifth.

The trade-off still applies: five wrong guesses against an email now show whether it has an account. If "go ahead" meant you wanted one of the mitigations I mentioned, tell me which one and I'll make it. Otherwise I can commit this change.
